rules.header_subtitle: Learn how the setup works, how turns progress, what the Executioner does, and how to win.
rules.step1_title: Step 1: Setting up Decks & Initial Cards
rules.step1_desc: Organize the play area by placing the Black Market (BM) deck on the left, line up the Plot Armor (PA) cards face up in the center by attribute color (Intelligence, Wisdom, Dexterity, and Strength) — note that their count equals the total number of players, e.g., if there are 2 players, there will be 2 Strength PA, 2 Intelligence PA, 2 Dexterity PA, and 2 Wisdom PA), and place the Executioner deck on the far right.
rules.step2_desc: Directly below the top row, set up the Death Line by placing the Main Deck (MD) on the far right. The significance of the Death Line is crucial, as whoever remains alive until the end wins:
rules.step2_list1: The Executioner: Always takes the very first position on the far left.
rules.step2_list2: The Three Peasants: Place all 3 Peasant cards immediately after the Executioner. They act as a protective buffer before any player is in danger.
rules.step2_list3: Character Selection: All players choose a character that represents them for the game. Shuffle the chosen Character cards and pick one at random to decide who starts first in the queue behind the Peasants.
rules.step2_list4: Seat Arrangement: Place the remaining player characters in order, following the natural seating order around the table in a clockwise direction. At the start of the game, each player gets 3 cards in hand from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.step3_desc: Directly below the Death Line, create the Board by drawing cards from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.step3_list1: Mathematical Formula: Deal exactly N + 2 cards onto the board, where N is the total number of players.
rules.step3_list2: Card Types: The board contains cards where Resource cards are face up, while Action cards are face down.
rules.phase1_desc: The game officially begins with the Draw Phase, the first of three phases in each round.
rules.phase1_list1: Turn Order: Players play strictly in the order they appear on the Death Line.
rules.phase1_list2: Card Selection: The first character in line chooses and draws one card of their choice directly from the available cards on the Board.
rules.phase1_list3: Empty Board Rule: If there are no available cards on the board when your turn comes, draw your card directly from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.phase1_complete_desc: Drawing continues along the line until every player has chosen one card from the board.
rules.phase1_complete_list1: Queue Sequence: After the first player, the next player in line takes their card, and so on.
rules.phase1_complete_list2: Board Reduction: As players take cards, the board will naturally shrink. Once all players have drawn a card, the Draw Phase ends.
rules.phase2_desc1: Once all players have drawn a card, the Action Phase begins according to the queue order, starting with the first player on the Death Line.
rules.phase2_desc2: On your turn, you can perform one of the following three main options:
rules.phase2_opt1: 1) Play an Action Card: Play a blue action card from your hand into your play area, immediately apply its effect, and then send it to the discard pile.
rules.phase2_opt2: 2) Purchase a Plot Armor Card: Discard 3 identical Resource cards + 1 Holy Duck Tape card from your hand to acquire the corresponding Plot Armor card. Note: The Plot Armor card does NOT go to the discard pile when you use its effect; it stays in front of you and you can use it once per round.
rules.phase2_opt2_ex: Example: Discarding 3 Wisdom resources and 1 Holy Duck Tape wins you a Wisdom Plot Armor card.
rules.phase2_opt3: 3) Purchase or Play a Black Market Card: Discard any 3 cards from your hand to take the top card from the Black Market deck.
rules.phase2_priority_title: Priority & Passing in the Action Phase
rules.phase2_priority_text1: During the Action Phase, each player takes one action on their turn, or they can choose to pass and do nothing.
rules.phase2_priority_text2: The Action Phase ends only when all players pass consecutively one after another.
rules.phase2_ex1_title: Example of Playing an Action Card
rules.phase2_ex1_text: The active player plays Unfair Trade to immediately execute its effect ("Draw 2 cards from the Main Deck"). Immediately after, the card goes to the discard pile as shown in the image below.
rules.phase2_ex2_text: To purchase a Strength Plot Armor card, surrender 3 Strength cards along with 1 Holy Duck Tape card.
rules.phase3_desc: When all players have passed, reveal the top card of the Executioner Deck. (Note: When the Executioner's cards run out, shuffle them to continue Phase 3 smoothly).
rules.phase3_list1: Board Replenishment: When the board needs replenishment, existing cards are not destroyed ("burned"), but empty slots are filled with cards from the Main Deck (MD) following the same formula (N + 2).
rules.phase3_list2: "YOU ARE UP NEXT": When this card is revealed, the Executioner executes the very next card in the Death Line.
rules.phase3_list3: Peasant Protection: The Executioner must first execute all 3 Peasants before any player character is in danger.
rules.phase3_list4: Flipping to Death State: When a player character dies, flip their card over to reveal the Death State artwork.
rules.phase3_ex1_text: Drawing "YOU'RE NEXT", the Executioner moves forward and executes the next target in line.
rules.phase3_ex2_text: Executed characters flip over to reveal their Death State.
rules.purpose_text1: Prove that you are the protagonist! The first player to collect 3 Plot Armor cards wins.
rules.purpose_text2: The Death Line matters and whoever remains alive wins. Alternatively, if all other players die, the last survivor wins immediately.

executioner.name: The Executioner
executioner.description: Beauty is a blessing and a curse. This is the problem of our story's beloved executioner. Male, female, and everything in between: if you want romantic company, you want the executioner. Legends say his first conquest was the midwife who delivered him. Having spent his entire life as the embodiment of the halo of beauty, he got tired. What is the point when everything and everyone is handed to you on a silver platter? So, he did the only thing that made sense: he decided he is a fighter, not a lover. Thus, he took over the family execution business and became the new executioner. Intertwined with death itself, people would surely stop looking at him just for his looks. With endless grace and sexuality, even in this, he finally succeeded. No longer just a sexy hunk. He is the sexy executioner.

notferatu.name: Notferatu
notferatu.description: A tough and ruthless vampire hunter. After his mother died from a vampire that cursed her blood, he vowed to dedicate his life to becoming the best vampire hunter in the world, so no one else would go through what he did. After years of training and finding the right equipment, he is ready to face a vampire... whenever he finds one. His latest trick? Dressing up as a vampire himself so that a real one would come out of hiding without fear... and then... then... the local peasants mistook him for a vampire and sent him to be executed. He holds garlic, wipes the makeup off his face, and shouts that he is a human hoping to be saved. Futile though, since everyone already knows he is human, they were just looking for an excuse to get rid of him for years because he drove everyone crazy with his vampire obsession.

misero.name: Misero
misero.description: Humor ages right along with a person. We don't know if that's true, but that is the current state of the king's once-beloved jester. After forty years of jokes, pie fights, and sarcasm, this clown stopped spreading smiles and joy. In a final attempt to become funny again, he decided to breathe new air into his presence by changing his stage name from Bozo to Laughie, Harley King, Gloom, and every other terrible name you can imagine, until he finally gave up and named himself Misero. Now, all he wants is to retire. But the king won't let him because, aside from being an unsurpassable performer/entertainer, he happens to be the king's only real advisor (when you're at court and no one counts you, you hear and learn a lot). Finally, he decided to go out the way he lived: with a joke. He made a particularly vulgar joke about the queen's backside and ended up in the execution line. He is happy with this development, but unfortunately for him, a child gave him a clown scepter and told him he is his biggest fan. Realizing he can still make someone laugh, he decides it's not his time yet.

paprika.name: Paprika
paprika.description: A young maid with a talent for cooking who, having minimal reading skills, finds a spice book with pictures and applies it to her next pie. She leaves everyone speechless as they taste the most gourmet medieval food of their lives. A woman being good at something, reading, and even using spices? She must be a witch! The court sentenced her to two months of community service, but she asked for execution instead because she is in love with the executioner (she believes she can ''change'' him). After driving the judge crazy for over 3 hours, he finally threw in the towel and sentenced her to death. Standing in the execution line, she unfortunately remembered that if the Executioner kills her, she will never see him again! So she decided to escape and change her approach.

hamlet.name: Hamlet
hamlet.description: It's the Middle Ages. A pig appears out of nowhere, pushes a flower pot off a lady's balcony, and it falls on the local lord's head, killing him instantly. You'd call that involuntary manslaughter or murder? Whether it's a pig doesn't matter... someone has to pay for this tragic accident. The worst part? The pig actually has intelligence and consciousness, specifically being a secret member and informant of an underground anti-regime organization. His plan all along was to assassinate this noble so the city would fall into the hands of this secret organization, all without trouble with the law! After all, who would accuse a pig? Everyone basically, because he forgot he was in the Middle Ages, and the prevailing notion is that animals have consciousness since criminal law is still in its infancy. Thus, a cunning conspirator now finds himself trying desperately not to become bacon.
